Umamusume: Pretty Derby is teaming up with the Denver Broncos for their clash against the Miami Dolphins, bringing Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen to the NFL in specially designed uniforms.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A woman has revealed that she completed seven marathons in 2026 despite being pregnant for a few of them, admitting that it was a bit “bizarre” at times.

For a lot of people, running a marathon is a goal that they work towards for months, if not years. Some want to set an impressive time, while others just want to be able to say they’ve completed the 26.2 miles.

In the case of Deirdre Keane, the 38-year-old is a seasoned long-distance runner, completing more than 60 marathons to this point. However, throughout 2026, she has been running marathons with an additional hurdle to deal with: she has been pregnant throughout.

“I knew how bizarre it was to be running a marathon at 34 weeks, but I also knew how fit I was and self-aware of my body at this point,” she told the Associated Press, admitting it is a “very unusual” challenge, but noted that she isn’t the first woman to do so.

As per the AP, the 38-year-old had signed up for 11 races in 2026, including the seven major marathons: Berlin, Boston, Chicago, London, Latest York, Sydney and Tokyo.

“I was like, this is going to be my last hurrah before settling down and becoming pregnant, becoming a mother,” Keane added. However, she didn’t discover she was pregnant until after running the Tokyo marathon, when she noticed her pace had started to slip.

“I don’t think she thought I would do them towards the end, especially being so pregnant at Fresh York. But I am very stubborn and determined,” Keane added. “Plus, I got lucky; I was feeling good. So I was able to do it.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A university in China has rolled out a $5 million surveillance system that actually checks if people are paying attention in class.

Plenty of schools across the globe have embraced technology in their classrooms. Some of these have been as simple as letting kids use iPads and computers, while other schools are fully focused on teaching students about AI. Others are even using AI-powered robots to help them teach.

So, these days, it can be pretty difficult to slack off, not pay attention to what your teacher is saying, and then grab some notes from your friend.

Over in China, though, things have been taken to the next level when it comes to checking on who is actually paying attention to the lessons.

As per the South China Morning Post, Nanjing University, in Jiangsu province, has rolled out a smart classroom system that monitors students in different ways.

The system, which cost just under $5 million, tracks attendance and lateness, but is also able to check the “head-raising rate” of students as well. If you’re not looking up at the teacher and paying attention, the system will recognise that and count it against you.

According to SCMP, some students have rallied against the system on social media, forcing the university to scrap the tracking of head-raising rates. However, that hasn’t stopped other schools from going ahead with it.

SCMP noted that the China University of Mining and Technology in Jiangsu tracks the “classroom status” of students. This identified students who checked their phones during class, as well as flagging some as being asleep – even though they had been collecting notes.

A school in the UK has sent staff out in a minibus to bring absent pupils to class during GTA 6’s launch week, while also offering a prize draw to students who attend every day.

GTA 6 is finally here, and for many, the allure of taking a sick day to sneak in some extra game time is proving too strong. In fact, some workplaces, like this California-based car company, gave employees the day off to play.

Sources indicate that an army unit in the United States even offered troops a four-day pass to play GTA 6 as part of their incentives to re-enlist, with 20 soldiers taking up the offer. According to ITV News, Ninestiles Academy in Birmingham has sent staff into the local community in a minibus to bring pupils to school during GTA 6’s launch week.

“We have been working hard to make this a particularly engaging and positive week for our learners, with a range of activities designed to encourage strong attendance,” mentioned principal Alex Hughes.

“This has included careers-focused assemblies and information events, colleagues visiting the local community in our school minibus to help bring learners into school and a prize draw for everyone who achieves 100% attendance across the week.”.

Ninestiles has not stated whether any pupils brought in by minibus missed class because they were playing GTA 6, but its more direct approach to tackling convenient absences around GTA 6’s launch is just one of several ways schools have responded.

Another school in England offered students the chance to win an $85 Amazon voucher for attending on launch day, while a professor in Spain actually canceled homework and postponed an exam to give students more time to play.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick is already being asked about GTA 7, despite GTA 6 only being days old.

Rockstar released GTA 6 on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait for a fresh numbered Grand Theft Auto.

But while players are only just getting their first look at Vice City and the rest of Leonida, some are already looking ahead to the next entry in the series.

On launch day, Zelnick joined the TBPN podcast to talk about the release, and was asked early on about when GTA 7 could drop, to which he answered: “Once you get through several hundred hours of the most incredible fun you’ve ever heard, ask the question again.”.

Later in the interview, he was asked about the sequel again and how substantial the map could be, given that GTA 6 covers a huge city and a surrounding state.

“Theoretically, GTA 7 could just be a live version of the entire world, right?” one of the hosts asked, with Zelnick clearly amused by the question.

According to recent reports, “We at Take-Two just went live with GTA 6 on November 19,” he jokingly replied. “Let me check my watch. Oh, it’s still November 19. And you’re asking a question about GTA 7. I mean guys, really?”.

Jordi: "Theoretically, GTA 7 could just be a live version of the entire world, right?"@StraussZelnick, the CEO behind GTA 6: "We went live with GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7." pic.twitter.com/sHdVawdln2.

He then mentioned a quote his father used to say about past achievements being “yesterday’s headlines,” but then quipped: “It’s not even yesterday.”.

With GTA 6 only just arriving, it will likely be years before we get any concrete information about its potential follow-up. However, Zelnick has hinted that Rockstar’s future games won’t take as long to make.

Plus, we still have GTA 6 Online to look forward to, which should tide players over until GTA 7.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A brand-newly introduced phone that doesn’t connect to the internet has been debuted in Japan, and it looks like the classic Nokia phones that you might remember.

For years, smartphone users have been trying to find creative solutions to cut down their screen time, especially as phones have started doing weekly reviews of app usage and screen time.

Some have opted to set time limits on the apps they can use, while others have created heavyweight cases that will quite literally force you to work out in order to use your smartphone.

It has been revealed that in other cases, some people have taken a step back in time, ditching their smartphones for flip phones and devices that don’t actually connect to the internet. These throwback phones have popped up across Europe and the United States, and now Japan is getting in on the act with a new device.

As per The Japan Times, Japan’s KDDI Corporation has introduced a mobile phone with “minimal functions.”.

Named the Infobar Zero, it will be available to pick up on Christmas Day, and is limited to calls, text messages, and other basic features. Owners won’t have the ability to connect to the internet, but it will have a camera and a music player.

While it isn’t a complete recreation of Nokia’s iconic 3310 phone, the Infobar Zero does strike up plenty of comparisons to that classic device.

Additionally, the ‘dumbphone’ isn’t aimed at replacing your smartphone, but rather providing a break from the smartphone life.

It has been planned by KDDI for quite some time, just as a way of relieving the reliance to live life on apps.

Owners will be able to register their phone numbers on the Zero and a smartphone as part of KDDI’s “two numbers” system – sort of like using an eSIM in some parts of the world.

  • GTA 6 players are reporting crashes on PS5 and Xbox, with some even unable to get past the opening minutes of the game.
  • While many GTA 6 fans across PlayStation and Xbox are enjoying their time in Leonida, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows for everyone trying to explore Rockstar’s latest installment.
  • Since its November 19 release, players have reported game-breaking crashes that prevent them from progressing through the main story and even playing altogether.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 players are reporting crashes on PS5 and Xbox, with some even unable to get past the opening minutes of the game.

While many GTA 6 fans across PlayStation and Xbox are enjoying their time in Leonida, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows for everyone trying to explore Rockstar’s latest installment.

Since its November 19 release, players have reported game-breaking crashes that prevent them from progressing through the main story and even playing altogether.

In a Reddit post, one PS5 player said the game had worked flawlessly until they reached Pipework, one of the game’s early missions, where you are introduced to Mandy.

Industry observers note that “It crashes every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it,” they wrote, adding that they can no longer progress through the story. “You would think the plane flying was intensive, but it crashes every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it. I just paid $125 for my PS5 to be repaired and $100 for the game, this is ridiculous.”.

Others are running into problems much earlier, with a PS5 Pro owner revealing the game crashes as the opening prologue begins.

“Game keeps crashing at the exact same point during the opening prologue. I’m using a PS5 Pro and have been unable to play since launch. The game crashes immediately as the startup prologue begins, either at the exact same point or a couple of seconds into it, displaying error code CE-108255-1.”.

When checking the PlayStation Support page, error CE-108255-1 prompts players to simply “try updating your game”. However, GTA 6 fans who have encountered this issue on PS5 have reported that clearing the console’s cache, rebuilding its database, factory resetting the PS5, and downloading the game three times has done nothing to alleviate the problem.

According to recent reports, “Despite all this, the glitch persists. It crashes at the same point every single time,” they wrote. “I’m honestly extremely disappointed and frustrated at this point. I’ve exhausted almost every troubleshooting step available online and still haven’t been able to play.”.

According to recent reports, the reports are not limited to PlayStation, either, as some Xbox Series X players have also reported crashes within minutes of play. “The game sometimes even crashes after only 15 minutes. The first crash happened about 2 hours after I started playing, and ever since that it kept crashing,” added another player.

Rockstar’s GTA 6 troubleshooting page currently directs players experiencing console errors to PlayStation or Xbox support, but hopefully a patch will fix this problem sooner rather than later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, animal control was forced to respond to a call about an alligator on the loose, but it turned out to be just a pool floatie. Seriously.

Over the years, plenty of people have rushed to call emergency services to report something that, when investigated, turned out to be totally false.

This was the case over in Sugar Land, Texas, on November 12 when animal control received a call about an alligator being on the loose. As per Sugar Land Animal Services, they were told that the gator appeared to be feeling a bit sick and in need of some assistance.

Sources indicate that yet, when they reached it, it wasn’t all it seemed. “When ASO Perez arrived on the scene to investigate, she was in for a big surprise. What looked very real from a distance turned out to be a runaway pool floatie!” they posted on Facebook.

“While this call definitely gave our team a good laugh, we always take every report seriously,” Animal Services added.

In the photo, the inflatable gator had its mouth stuck open with teeth on show, so if you see it from a distance, you might be confused. However, up close, you can tell it’s meant to be lounged on, not hunted or scared of.

Industry observers note that “Remember: if you ever spot wildlife that looks sick or injured, please keep a safe distance and call the experts to handle it. You never know if it’s the real deal!”.

Naturally, commenters saw the funny side of things too. “Well, that was a rather inflated story then,” one joked. “She is very brave! Thank you, Officer Perez, for all you do,” another added. “Wow. It looks so realistic! Crazy,” another replied.

As noted, it isn’t the first instance of floaties being reported as real, nor is it the wildest.

The fast food chain announced on November 20 that its Back Home BOGO deal will return for one night only, allowing Rewards members to get two meals for the price of one at participating US restaurants.

Recent findings suggest that the promotion first introduced in 2025 and became Chipotle’s largest sales-driving campaign of the year. Its return comes as millions of Americans prepare to travel home and reconnect with friends and family over Thanksgiving weekend.

On Wednesday, November 25, Chipotle Rewards members can receive a free meal when purchasing another one of equal or greater value between 5 p.m. and 9 p.m. local time.

To redeem the offer, customers must visit a participating US Chipotle restaurant and scan their Rewards membership card at checkout.

The promotion is available exclusively in restaurants, meaning orders placed through the Chipotle app, website, delivery services, or third-party platforms will not qualify.

Customers can receive up to five free meals per check, provided they purchase an meal of equal or greater value for each free item. Kids’ meals do not count toward the promotion.

“Thanksgiving Eve is when the hometown group chat comes to life,” noted Stephanie Perdue, Chipotle’s Senior Vice President of Brand Marketing.

According to recent reports, “Whether Chipotle is the first stop of the night or where the crew ends up later, we’re giving friends a place to get together over real food. The response last year highlighted us how much our guests embraced the occasion, and we’re excited to bring it back as another reason for hometown crews to reconnect before Thanksgiving.”.

Chipotle releases School Spirit BOGO with free entrees for back-to-school season.

The company cited Morning Consult research showing that 76% of Gen Z consumers visit restaurants to socialize with friends and family, highlighting the role dining out plays in holiday gatherings.

Chipotle is also offering a separate promotion following Thanksgiving, giving customers a $0 delivery fee on qualifying orders from November 27 through November 30.

To claim the delivery offer, customers must enter the code CYBER26 when ordering through Chipotle’s app or website. The deal requires a minimum purchase of $10 in the US or $12 in Canada, excluding taxes and fees.

Although the delivery fee will be waived, customers may still face higher menu prices and additional service fees.

Both promotions are available for a limited time at participating locations, with the Thanksgiving BOGO ending at 9 p.m. local time on November 25.

Taco Bell is bringing back a discontinued menu item after a decade, with the fast-food chain confirming that one of its former burritos will return to restaurants nationwide in 2027.

The announcement comes as Taco Bell continues to revive older menu items, including the Quesarito, Flamin’ Hot Grilled Cheese Burrito, and Cheesy Street Chalupas, which have recently returned for limited-time runs.

Industry observers note that however, the latest comeback wasn’t decided by Taco Bell executives. Instead, the organization allowed fans to choose which discontinued item would return as part of its inaugural Live Más Open golf tournament, hosted by comedian Kevin Hart.

Taco Bell has confirmed that the Steakhouse Boss Burrito will return to participating US restaurants for a limited time in 2027, marking its first appearance since 2016.

Originally introduced as the Steakhouse Burrito, the returning item features a warm flour tortilla filled with a choice of grilled, marinated steak or marinated all-white-meat chicken.

The burrito includes twice the amount of meat found in Taco Bell’s Steak Grilled Cheese Burrito, along with warm queso sauce, bacon, seasoned potatoes, and reduced-fat sour cream.

It also features a three-cheese blend consisting of mozzarella, pepper jack, and cheddar.

The decision to bring back the burrito came during Taco Bell’s Live Más Open, which took place at The Ranch at Laguna Beach in California earlier this month.

The nine-hole golf tournament featured celebrities, athletes, and Taco Bell fans competing for the opportunity to revive a discontinued menu item.

Team Pink, consisting of Taco Bell fan Abby Abel, professional skateboarder Sean Malto, influencer Emira D’Spain, and reality television personality Serena Page, secured the victory following a sudden-death putting playoff against Team White.

Taco Bell is making fans win a golf tournament to bring back a discontinued menu item.

Their prize included championship jackets, a trophy, and the opportunity to select a former Taco Bell menu item for a nationwide comeback.

The tournament also featured a Taco Bell drive-thru on the golf course, serving exclusive items including the Fire Piña Hot Dog, Baja Caesar Crispy Chicken Crunchwrap, and Fiesta Potato Salad.

The Live Más Open is available to stream on Peacock beginning November 20, with a television broadcast scheduled for November 23 on Golf Channel.

Taco Bell has not announced an exact release date or pricing for the Steakhouse Boss Burrito, although the tech giant confirmed it will be available nationwide for a limited time in 2027.

The announcement follows several other menu changes from Taco Bell, including the return of the Quesarito and the upcoming Make It Flamin’ Hot customization option, which will allow customers to add Flamin’ Hot Fritos to eligible menu items beginning November 24.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s a latest vibe-coded OS in town going by the name of LiberNT.
  • LiberNT has been under development for some time, but on Wednesday it made a massive leap.
  • This still fledgling operating system is designed (mostly) for modern hardware and focuses on 64-bit platforms: amd64, arm64 and riscv64.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s a latest vibe-coded OS in town going by the name of LiberNT. Its name provides a big clue to its nature: Liber (free), NT (New Technology architecture, as in Windows NT). As it has been released under GNU’s GPL3.0 license, LiberNT also provides a free new way to run apps designed for Microsoft’s Windows 11.

LiberNT has been under development for some time, but on Wednesday it made a massive leap. Reading the intro, you might have wondered if this work had a ReactOS connection, and indeed there is. But what started as a fork of ReactOS has already got a new boot loader, graphics stack, memory manager – and yesterday a new kernel. “LiberNT is not affiliated with or endorsed by the ReactOS project or Microsoft,” insist the devs behind this OS.

This still fledgling operating system is designed (mostly) for modern hardware and focuses on 64-bit platforms: amd64, arm64 and riscv64. Ambitiously, the goal is to develop this OS to deliver a free Windows alternative that is “stable, reliable and efficient.” On that latter point, yesterday’s blog update relays some impressive efficiency and performance stats.

The LiberNT team has benchmarked their eponymous OS against Microsoft’s Windows NT, and it beats it hands-down in 112 of 132 system tests. The testing assessed performance in the following areas: file caching, memory handling, threads and locks, plus FAT32 and NTFS storage. Interestingly, both the free and commercial OS were benchmarked on a Mac with an Apple M3 Pro chip. We scanned through the results, and the worst loss for LiberNT was a 28% performance deficit vs Win11, but it claims some astounding relative performance wins showing the free OS being over 2000% faster.

The devs are entirely clear about the fact that the operating system was vibe coded. “AI is part of how LiberNT is built. It helps us review and write code, and everything it writes is then reviewed by a human,” explains a section of the GitHub page for the project. “Before anything reaches the main branch, a person runs and validates the end-to-end tests. We care about this project too much to let a regression slip through.”.

If the above highlights about this fresh OS's scope, mission, compatibility, and performance have whetted your appetite, there is the full code available via the GitHub link (top), and even some ready-made builds as bootable disk images. Indeed, I’m quite eager to give this new OS a spin. Hopefully, it works as well as the ambitious developers suggest, and I won’t be disappointed by any stability concerns using my daily productivity apps like Firefox, Word, and an old release of Photoshop.

A former Supermicro employee was also quoted in the complaint saying that it was “widely known within the Organization that Chen had to leave because she had sent emails requesting that Nvidia release chips with serial numbers associated with the GPUs illegally diverted to customers in China.” This apparently refers to the serial numbers that were moved from real to dummy servers using a hairdryer.

Recent findings suggest that supermicro has mentioned multiple times that it has cooperated with the U.S. government regarding the smuggling investigation and that it has not been included in the lawsuit against the three defendants. Furthermore, the firm has denied her involvement regarding Nvidia GPU allocations. “Chen did not manage Supermicro’s relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers,” a Supermicro spokesperson told The Information. They also said that she left voluntarily and that her LinkedIn profile now reads her current position as CEO of ChronoScale, an Nvidia cloud partner based in Silicon Valley. As for Puri, he stepped away from his position at Nvidia in late August, about two months before the Jensen Huang scandal blew up, although he remains as an advisor to the AI chipmaker.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, intel has reduced its workforce by approximately 27,800 employees under Lip-Bu Tan, based on the firm's reported headcount figures, but this does not seem to be enough.
  • The latest cuts in Intel's IT organization reportedly began on November 16, although Intel has not disclosed how many employees will lose their jobs, notes TrendForce citing CTech.
  • It has been revealed that the latest reductions follow several rounds of layoffs throughout 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, intel has reduced its workforce by approximately 27,800 employees under Lip-Bu Tan, based on the firm's reported headcount figures, but this does not seem to be enough. The company has reportedly initiated another round of layoffs, this time across its global information technology (IT) organization, as its chief executive continues to reduce expenses and simplify the company's operations, reports Business Insider.

The latest cuts in Intel's IT organization reportedly began on November 16, although Intel has not disclosed how many employees will lose their jobs, notes TrendForce citing CTech. Some employees claim that the reductions could affect a double-digit percentage of the department's workforce of around 2,607 people at 55 sites in 53 countries, so we are talking about at least 260 people if we are talking about a 10% reduction, or as much as 520 if we are talking about a 20% reduction. One has to keep in mind that these estimates have not been independently verified. Intel has neither confirmed the number of affected employees nor identified the specific teams involved. Instead, the company reiterated to Business Insider that it regularly reviews its workforce to ensure that personnel and financial resources correspond to its strategic priorities.

It has been revealed that the latest reductions follow several rounds of layoffs throughout 2026. In July, Intel eliminated positions in its Data Center and AI Group. Between July and October, the company submitted nine Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) notices in California, which covered 222 employees, according to Business Insider. The most recent notice, filed on October 22, concerned 67 permanent job cuts at Intel's Folsom campus (which mostly specializes in R&D, hardware validation, and software development), effective October 31. As of November 17, no additional WARN notices had been reported.

It has been revealed that intel employed 81,100 people as of September 27, 2026, including 76,500 employees at Intel itself and another 4,600 at Mobileye and other subsidiaries. This compares with 85,100 employees at the end of 2025 and 108,900 a year earlier, which means that the company's workforce declined by 4,000 since December, 2025, and 27,800 since December, 2024. respectively.

Intel's workforce reductions began well before Lip-Bu Tan became chief executive in 2025. In 2024, his predecessor Pat Gelsinger declared intends to eliminate more than 15,000 positions, or approximately 15% of the company’s workforce. Tan has continued to reduce expenses, eliminate management layers, and discontinue lower-priority projects as Intel attempts to cut costs and reduce losses/improve profitability.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI data center build-out is pushing electricity grids across the globe, with many regions facing demand from projects that would exceed the current peak load that each system could support. According to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) World Energy Outlook 2026 report, a total of 120GW of capacity is at the moment available across all types of data centers across the globe, with another 120GW expected to be completed by the end of the decade, 75% of which would be dedicated to artificial intelligence. Aside from that, it’s also tracking 93 large “AI factories” that are either under construction or being expanded via satellite imagery. It estimates that the capacity for these sites grew from under 2GW to 17GW in just two years, and that they’re expected to hit a total of 50GW upon completion, the equivalent of adding a second Great Britain to power demand.

Industry observers note that this massive power consumption is one of the reasons for the opposition against their construction in communities, with residents blaming them for increased utility prices. However, the IEA claims that its analysis “does not yet show a clear relationship between growth in data center capacity and increases in electricity prices.” It noted that if a data center uses existing capacity and pays for its share of the cost, then it could potentially lead to lower utility bills for all customers. However, if the grid operator is required to upgrade its system to accommodate the large consumer, then it could also lead to increased monthly bills if the costs are spread across all people.

Industry observers note that emissions are another issue that the IEA has raised. Renewable energy dominates data centers’ power purchase agreements at nearly 50%, but actual power generation puts coal- and natural-gas power sources closer to 60%. This is likely due to the need for reliability, with the latter kicking in when the former cannot deliver the power that the data center needs. Aside from that, a few projects are deploying their own power, like Elon Musk’s Colossus 2 in Southaven, Mississippi, with about 180GW planned or under construction in the U.S. So, even though renewable energy is growing to accommodate demand, it’s also expected that coal- and natural-gas emissions from data centers will rise by 70% by 2030.

Investments in AI data centers are expected to hit $32 trillion by 2050, putting the infrastructure spending for the industry larger than railways, electrification, and the internet, combined. Despite that, the IEA says the grid remains a significant bottleneck — renewable power plants take between one and five years to complete, which is around the same time that some massive data center projects take if they do not face an extended moratorium, while transmission works can take three to five times longer. This is probably one of the reasons why some AI hyperscalers are choosing to put jet engines on their sites instead, although these are also facing shortages, especially in turbine blades.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A North Carolina woman was evicted from her apartment after an AI leasing assistant mistakenly told her she could delay paying nearly $4,000 in overdue rent.

Laura Mack, a resident of Colony Townhome Apartments in Raleigh, received an email on November 8 asking when she could pay her outstanding balance of $3,934.17.

Mack responded that she wanted to pay on November 30 and received written confirmation that the date was acceptable. However, eight days later, she was served with an eviction notice.

When Mack contacted the leasing office, she noted an employee explained that the emails had been sent by Olivia, the apartment complex’s AI assistant, which had mistakenly approved her request.

The complex had introduced Olivia to residents in December 2025, explaining that the assistant could answer questions about rent and maintenance around the clock.

Although previous emails from Olivia had been clearly identified as AI-generated, the November 8 messages were signed by Colony Townhome Apartments and did not disclose that they had been written by a chatbot.

Mack remarked she believed she was communicating with a member of staff, particularly because the emails referenced a bathroom ceiling leak that had taken almost two weeks to repair.

“I thought it was someone from the office because all my information was in there and it mentioned my bathroom,” she told WRAL.

Despite having the agreement in writing, Mack was evicted on November 19. She subsequently stayed in a hotel while trying to determine her next steps.

“If you told me till the 30th, I’ll get out by the 30th,” she said. “But give me that. You at least honor that. You have to have somewhere where you’re taking responsibility.”.

In a recent development, north Carolina state Sen. Jim Burgin subsequently commented on the case, calling the situation “ridiculous.”.

“Before someone evicted that lady, they should have reviewed their documents,” he told WRAL in a follow-up to the original story.

A spokesperson for Colony Townhome Apartments told the site that the property’s owners were gathering information about the eviction and expected to provide an enhancement at a later date.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that considering the current status of the cybersecurity landscape, some may well say that "0-day" has lost its meaning, The latest high-stakes vulnerability pertains to a bug in Windows 11 (and possibly 10), wherein an attacker can partially bypass the lock screen and run software as the logged-in user, and seemingly access their data.
  • It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, the bug was discovered by Abdelhamid Naceri, the prolific Windows hacker known to the world as Nightmare Eclipse, and is responsible for about a dozen zero-day findings in Microsoft's operating system.
  • In a recent development, to trigger the vulnerability, all you need is a keyboard.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that considering the current status of the cybersecurity landscape, some may well say that "0-day" has lost its meaning, The latest high-stakes vulnerability pertains to a bug in Windows 11 (and possibly 10), wherein an attacker can partially bypass the lock screen and run software as the logged-in user, and seemingly access their data. If true, the vulnerability means even BitLocker won't help keep customers' files protected.

It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, the bug was discovered by Abdelhamid Naceri, the prolific Windows hacker known to the world as Nightmare Eclipse, and is responsible for about a dozen zero-day findings in Microsoft's operating system. The exploit requires physical access to the machine, but that's precisely the scenario that lock screens and/or BitLocker are supposed to protect against.

In a recent development, to trigger the vulnerability, all you need is a keyboard. In the Windows 11 lock screen, click "Forgot my PIN," then hit Win+U to bring up the voice narrator. The window will be hidden behind the lock screen, which, for practical purposes, is just a veneer, but you can interact with it using the keyboard if you hold down the Caps Lock key and use the arrows and Enter.

After some brief navigation through Narrator, you'll actually be in Settings, and then have multiple avenues for further shenanigans. One obvious one is going into Bluetooth and Devices and setting Autoplay to show a USB stick's files and folders, then plugging in your own with your software of choice to run. Additionally, on a personal machine, the user is bound to have administrator permissions, so you can just create your own account.

Industry observers note that this bug is quite fresh, so there isn't widespread reporting or testing. The author claims "the vulnerability seems to be extremely consistent in every machine I tested it in." We did encounter a sysadmin on Reddit, danrhodes1987, who claims they've tested it on machines they manage, and sure enough, it works, though only on their InTune-enrolled devices. He says that "you can launch anything you want in the context of the user logged onto the device.".

In a recent development, additionally, they found it possible to invisibly navigate whichever programs the user had open before they locked their screen, which all but guarantees that the victim's entire data and programs will be fully accessible. As a Windows sysadmin friend of mine remarked, Windows' lock screen implementation always felt like a kludge, and he posits this won't be the last hack found for it.

GTA 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake are being hit with waves of zero-score user reviews on Metacritic, with fans of each game appearing to target the other.

The two share more than a fanbase rivalry, as GTA 6 landed a 99 Metascore at launch, tying the original 1998 Ocarina of Time for the highest critic score in the site’s history.

While critics have been near-unanimous in their praise, GTA 6’s user score on PlayStation 5 has fallen to 5.0, with thousands of negative ratings arriving within a day of launch.

That’s in stark contrast to the PlayStation Store, where ratings can only be left by players who own the game, and GTA 6 currently holds a score of 4.84 out of 5.

People like this are so lazy. Metacritic is not the only place that owners can rate games. But it IS one of the most accessible (meaning it's susceptible to review bombing).PS5 players can rate the games in the Playstation store, and it's at the moment at 4.84/5. https://t.co/BBo090644U pic.twitter.com/s3X7YnbjGX.

Some of the accounts leaving zero scores on Metacritic have barely rated anything else, with Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time remake the only other game on their profile, scored a perfect 10.

One of those reviews blasted Rockstar for “making us wait 13 years for an 80-100$ (maybe invisible or stolen) code in a box that only runs at 30 FPS,” calling it “a buggy mess at launch.”.

Another took aim at the game’s £100 ($132) digital-only price, adding, “This is the beginning of the end for Sony and Rockstar.”.

The Ocarina of Time remake rolled out on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, and by November 8 held a 9.6 user score, the highest in Metacritic’s history.

Sources indicate that that has since dropped to 9.0, with a fresh batch of zero scores aimed squarely at Nintendo fans. “Fan forever GTA 6. Go cry fans of Zelda,” one read.

Others were more direct about why they were leaving them, with one zero-score review simply reading, “Y’all losers review bombing GTA 6.”.

GTA 6 is the joint best-reviewed game of all-time.

Zelda Ocarina of Time remake sells 5.2 million copies in four days to break Switch 2 record.

GTA 6 fans concerned for game following major Rockstar leak.

It isn’t clear which side started it, with GTA 6 fans claiming Nintendo players flooded Rockstar’s game first, and some Zelda fans insisting it was the other way around.

Not every negative GTA 6 review is part of the feud, with some players taking concern with the game’s 30fps cap on consoles, frame rate drops, and open-world bugs.

Others have objected to the game’s optional romance system and claimed GTA 6 has gone “woke,” while some simply called it “the biggest disappointment in gaming history.”.

Unlike the PlayStation Store, Metacritic doesn’t require customers to prove they own a game before leaving a rating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that videos of an incredibly acrobatic, nimble, and graceful John Deere 5-ton skid-steer loader have been shared by a group of researchers from the U.S. and Switzerland. A recently published paper titled Heavy Metal Acrobatics provides the reasoning behind this eyebrow-raising autonomous robotics feat. It is hoped this research will be useful in the future automation of heavy machinery in industries like construction, mining, and material handling. It also demonstrates that reinforcement learning in a simulation can transfer remarkably well to the real world.

Researchers have used reinforcement learning to teach a 5-tonne John Deere skid-steer loader to perform complex acrobatic manoeuvres autonomously. Trained in simulation and transferred to a real machine, the system can balance on two wheels, navigate rough terrain, spin, and control its bucket before landing safely. The research demonstrates the potential of AI-driven automation for heavy construction and industrial machinery. Video Credit: @leggedrobotics / @ETH Paper: https://t.co/MT7fyZ54Hk #engineering #technologyNovember 17, 2026.

If you unfurl the video embed above, you can see a hulking 332G skid-steer do some astonishing tricks. It hops back and forth on two wheels, pirouettes, and balances while flexing its lift arm. Moreover, it does these moves while never looking like it will teeter over. The researchers claim that “only a handful of elite human operators” have ever been able to pull off stunts as you see in the demo videos.

Recent findings suggest that the technology behind the remarkable acrobatic skid-steer is mostly Reinforcement Learning (RL), with physics modeling and neural network models. As machinery like this is so massive, powerful, and bulky, undertaking RL directly on the hardware wasn’t deemed practical. Instead, the research team decided to use a simulation programmed with the John Deere 332G’s complex array of controls for training. This data was subsequently applied to the actual skid-steer via a sim-to-real transfer. The simulations must be extremely accurate.

This acrobatic goliath is impressive, but of course there’s an underlying goal driving Heavy Metal Acrobatics’ research. The scientists are laying the foundations for the enabling of “dynamic autonomous control of heavy machinery.” It is hoped this will help promote greater automation in heavy equipment sectors of industry. Eventually, autonomous control should be safer, faster, and more efficient than any human.

In a recent development, with these video demonstrations of nimble and highly maneuverable heavy machinery, it is clear that there’s more scope for AI-driven automation than one may have previously expected. Furthermore, it looks like being a skilled heavy machinery operator is definitely not an AI-proof occupation.

  • OpenAI claims that its model spotted "further improvements by rewriting the code that describes the chip’s circuits." This work was done in SystemVerilog RTL, the language commonly used for high-end chip design.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, openAI just revealed latest details about its ongoing partnership with AMD, in which engineers used undisclosed AI models to help optimize the hardware maker's upcoming flagship GPU and CPU designs. The leading figures are up to 14% PPA (power, performance, and area) improvement for the GPU circuitry, and unspecified single-digit PPA gains on the processor.

OpenAI claims that its model spotted "further improvements by rewriting the code that describes the chip’s circuits." This work was done in SystemVerilog RTL, the language commonly used for high-end chip design. The firm claims that its model's optimization efforts are equivalent to condensing a year's worth of conventional chip design work into "under 5 months" — a time crunch it says is unprecedented in this arena.

Furthermore, OpenAI indicates its model was reasoning on RTL "at the level of an expert microarchitect," and that it expects to squeeze further PPA improvements in both GPU and CPU designs, up from the now-improved baseline.

In a recent development, this isn't AI's first time working on chips. It worked with Broadcom on designing OpenAI Jalapeño, an inference-targeted chip that was already running actual workloads with engineering samples as far back as June 2026.

The tech giant expected to have small initial Jalapeño deployments around late 2026, and pinned a broader rollout to 2027. Test benchmarks have been out for a while, displaying purported excellent savings on power draw and overall latency versus the market-leading Nvidia Blackwell GPUs in single-token prediction workloads.

According to recent reports, the blog post also explains how GPT's chip-design acumen evolved. The researchers tested its high-end LLMs by asking them to improve PicoRV32 and Ibex chip cores. The models were given 112,000 tokens per run, told to optimize for throughput (a combination of Instructions-per-Clock and clock-cycle duration), and scored the results.

Industry observers note that A fat zero was given if the chips didn't work or used more than 16x the previous area, and 1.0 was given for the best designs under the test constraints. The test also didn't tell the models which workloads the chips were going to be used for. As expected, GPT-6.2 Astra had by far the best showing, on both axes: both the lowest overall cost and the highest optimization score.

A second test also revealed an interesting but unsurprising fact: the models provided better results when essentially redesigning the chips according to their initial specifications, rather than optimizing existing code.

There's no word on whether the scientists used unmodified versions of GPT to perform this work. Task-specific high-end LLMs exist for those who can afford them, and OpenAI itself notes it's working with Synopsys to train GPT-Synopsis, a model for using chip design tools.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

In a recent development, 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Getting shortlisted for a junior data analyst job depends less on how many courses you have finished and more on what you can show. This initiative breaks preparation into eight skill areas, pairs each one with a learning option and a hands-on task, and gives you a simple test for knowing when to move on.

Many people preparing for their first analyst role study for months and still struggle to get interviews. Their CVs list SQL, Excel and Tableau, yet nothing on the page shows those tools being used to answer a real question. Recruiters reading dozens of similar applications need something more concrete.

According to recent reports, A course can give your learning a sensible order, but a completion badge says little about how you think. A small analysis that states its question, explains its method and admits its limits tells a hiring manager far more. This proposal aims to collect that kind of proof while you learn, not after.

Sources indicate that start by collecting ten to twenty entry-level postings in the industry you want to join, and tally the tools and tasks they mention. You will swiftly see a pattern. Some roles are built around Excel and routine reporting, while others want SQL, a BI platform and a bit of Python.

The wider market follows a similar shape. Jobright’s 2026 analysis of data analyst hiring, which looked at 2025–2026 postings from LinkedIn, Indeed and Levels.fyi, found that more than 80% of data analyst jobs mention SQL, over 60% mention Excel or Google Sheets, and roughly half mention Python or R. Let your own tally decide the order you learn in, but expect SQL to sit near the top.

As you work through each area below, finish with something you can show someone: a query, a tidied dataset, a chart, a one-page report or a portfolio project. Free material is often enough if you can stay disciplined. Pay for teaching only when it gives you something you cannot get alone, such as feedback, accountability or a fixed timetable.

SQL is how analysts pull, join and summarise records from a database, and a tool like Tableau lets other people explore what you found. Treat them as one workflow rather than two subjects: frame a question, write the query, sanity-check the numbers and present the result so a non-technical reader can follow it.

SQLBolt offers free, bite-sized SQL lessons that run in the browser, and Tableau publishes free training videos on connecting to data and building dashboards. Used together, they are enough to produce a small end-to-end project.

If you learn better with a set schedule and an instructor checking your work, you could learn to analyse data with SQL and Tableau from scratch through a guided programme at Heicoders Academy in Singapore. Whichever route you take, compare what is covered, how feedback is given, when sessions run and the full cost against what free resources already offer.

Proof you can show: A working SQL query set and your first published dashboard.

Move on when: You can take a question from idea to dashboard on your own, without following a tutorial line by line.

Spreadsheets are still where much of a team’s day-to-day reporting lives, especially when colleagues don’t write SQL. Get comfortable with filtering, pivot tables, and lookup functions, and learn to spot quiet errors like dates saved as text or one category spelled three different ways.

The next step is automating the cleanup so it doesn’t have to be repeated by hand each month. Microsoft’s Power Query documentation highlights how to import and reshape data in recorded steps that refresh when new data arrives. The same ideas apply in other spreadsheet tools too.

Proof you can show: A messy export turned into a summary that refreshes itself.

Move on when: You can clean an untidy CSV and build a report that updates when the source file changes.

In a recent development, for most junior analyst roles, the technical interview is a SQL test. Basic SELECT statements won’t be enough; interviewers like to probe joins, subqueries, common table expressions and window functions, which answer everyday questions such as running totals or each customer’s first purchase.

Practise with timed problem sets and review your answers for correctness as well as speed.

Proof you can show: Confidence going into a live or take-home SQL test.

Move on when: You can solve intermediate problems in around 15 to 20 minutes each without looking up syntax.

Take-home assignments often come with data that has been made messy on purpose. Reviewers want to see how you deal with missing values, duplicates and inconsistent formats, and whether they can follow your reasoning afterwards.

Keep a short cleaning log as you work, noting each change and why you made it. A separate sheet tab or a list of comments in a notebook both work.

Proof you can show: A take-home submission a reviewer can audit step by step.

Move on when: Every change to your dataset is written down with a reason.

It has been revealed that case-study questions test whether you can read numbers sensibly, not just produce them. A working grasp of distributions, means and medians, spread, correlation and sampling will keep you away from the mistakes that undo otherwise good answers, such as quoting an average that a few extreme values have pulled out of shape.

Proof you can show: Clear, careful answers in case-study interviews.

Move on when: You can explain in everyday language why two things moving together doesn’t mean one causes the other.

Every chart should help someone answer a specific question. Learn where bars, lines, scatter plots and simple tables each work best, and how axis ranges, labels and colour can nudge a reader towards the wrong conclusion. On a dashboard, the most vital finding should be the first thing people see.

In a recent development, datawrapper’s guidance on picking chart types is a useful free reference. As practice, show the same result in two different chart types and decide which one represents the data more honestly.

Proof you can show: Portfolio charts that make a point, not just show off features.

Move on when: A person who has never seen your data can spot the main finding and its caveat at a glance.

What counts as a useful metric depends on the role. Marketing analysts focus on conversion and retention, operations analysts on delivery times and capacity, and finance analysts on margins and cash flow. Choose one sector and learn exactly how its key measures are defined.

Proof you can show: A project built around the questions your target industry actually asks.

Move on when: You can define several sector metrics and describe how a manager would use each one.

Your portfolio is where the other seven areas come together. Two or three deep, well-documented projects will say more about you than a long list of quick ones. Give each project a README that sets out the question, the data, your method, the findings and the limitations.

Proof you can show: A portfolio link and a write-up you can talk through in an interview.

Move on when: Every project clearly explains what it asked, how you answered it and what you found.

According to recent reports, there is no need to finish all eight areas before you apply. Once you can use the tools your target roles mention, speak honestly about your work and point to two or three clearly explained projects, start sending applications and keep learning alongside them.

Recent findings suggest that adjust each application to the job. Lead with a reporting example for spreadsheet-heavy roles, a query that solved a real problem for SQL roles, and a chart that supported a decision for visualisation roles. Be upfront about which work you built independently and which came from guided exercises.

Recent findings suggest that do I really need eight courses? No. These are skill areas, not eight required qualifications. A single resource can cover several of them, and practice you do on your own counts as much as classroom learning.

Is it possible to prepare using only free material? Yes. Free tutorials, open textbooks, official documentation and public datasets cover the fundamentals well. The harder parts are sticking to a routine and finding people who will give you honest feedback.

According to recent reports, which should come first, SQL or spreadsheets? It depends on the jobs you want. Spreadsheets are an easy starting point for reporting roles, while SQL is expected wherever databases are involved. You will want both eventually, so start with whichever your target postings stress most.

How many portfolio projects should I have? Two or three solid ones are a good start. Each should show a clear question, steps someone else could repeat and an honest reading of the results, rather than several near-identical dashboards.

Sources indicate that do I need a certificate before I apply? Not usually. Some employers ask for one, but many judge skills through interviews, take-home tasks and tests instead. Go by what each posting actually requires.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Redditor from the UK was flying from the United States with their desktop PC in a carry-on but was forced to check it. According to u/FattyLeopold, they’ve carried their PC as a carry-on on different flights, and they brought it with them in the cabin all the way across the Atlantic. The trip even included a layover.

“It was 4am, and I was pissed off,” the Redditor replied to one comment. “Just said fu-- it, let’s see what happens. Probably confused the universe a bit, ‘Dude… what are you doing… Aight, have it your way.’” They then taped the PC, monitor, and keyboard together in the package.

Recent findings suggest that the desktop PC only had a bag and several layers of protective wrapping for protection. What’s more surprising is that the owner didn’t even take the GPU off its bracket and put it in their carry-on. When they arrived at their destination, they recorded the “unboxing” of their PC. Against all odds, their computer arrived without a single dent or scratch — the tempered glass on the side of the PC didn’t even shatter after the possible trauma it went through in baggage handling.

Most of us have seen videos of airport baggage handlers throwing bags and packages around while they’re loading them onto the plane, not to mention the bumps and tumbles that luggage takes when going through an airport’s baggage conveyor system. The PC also has to deal with the vibration and turbulence of flight. The shortest direct flight across the pond is about 6 hours and 30 minutes — since the Redditor said that they had a layover, that meant that the desktop PC had been in transit for a bit longer than that.

It’s a miracle that the computer was able to make it through the journey without a scratch, but the Redditor is not out of the woods yet. They noted that even though the computer looked undamaged on the surface, they haven’t been able to boot it yet because they do not have a proper adapter for outlets in the UK. Hopefully, they could get it working after finding the right plug or adapter for their computer, or with some basic troubleshooting (like re-plugging the components) if it won’t turn on after the first try. GPUs and memory sticks are quite expensive these days, after all, and it’s unlikely that AMD would replace their graphics card because of this misadventure, unlike this $10,000 RTX Pro 6000 that Nvidia replaced after a customer who bought it new broke the GPU in transit.

A group of elderly residents at a retirement home in France have been introduced GTA 6, and some are already hoping to get their hands on the game for Christmas.

Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 finally released on November 19, 2026, more than 13 years after the release of GTA 5.

The open-world crime game has attracted enormous attention worldwide, with fans taking time off work to play it. According to French broadcaster TF1, requests for annual leave in France increased by 8% around the game’s launch. Now, the game has been introduced to the older generations.

On November 20, residents at the Domitys senior living facility in Serris, Seine-et-Marne, were introduced to GTA 6 as part of an organized gaming session.

As reported by ICI Paris Île-de-France, the residents swapped their usual activities for an opportunity to explore the game’s virtual world, with many particularly enjoying its boat-driving sequences.

82-year-old Jacqueline was among the most enthusiastic participants, successfully collecting two packages of cocaine during a mission. “I had never touched a controller before 9am this morning. And by 2:30pm, I was fishing out two packages of drugs,” she joked.

Another resident, 86-year-old Lucienne, was equally impressed by the game’s visuals, describing them as incredible and comparing the experience to watching a real film.

Meanwhile, 75-year-old Yvan admitted that the controls were difficult to master, joking that he was no longer 20 and struggled to keep up with the action.

Staff explained that the residents had found driving and shooting particularly challenging, but enjoyed exploring the environment by boat.

The experience proved popular enough that Lucienne remarked she intended to ask her children for GTA 6 for Christmas, while Jacqueline suggested installing a console in the communal lounge.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Sources indicate that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

According to recent reports, 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Industry observers note that A self-hosted LLM gateway sits between your app and the model provider, so every call pays for one extra hop. We measured that cost for three open-source gateways: the Langfuse AI Gateway, the LiteLLM proxy and AcruxCore. Each one ran on the same machine, in front of the same OpenAI model. LiteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to every non-streaming call. AcruxCore added 15 to 24 ms. Langfuse's number could not be told apart from zero.

The bigger lesson was about the measurement itself. Before we controlled for it, one OpenAI network address moved our results by more than any gateway did.

Each number is the median time a gateway added to a direct OpenAI call, with its 95% interval in brackets. A gateway can log each call, and logging takes time, so we ran the test three times with three logging levels.

In a recent development, the direct call took 781 to 831 ms at the median, so even LiteLLM's cost is under 9% of a short call. Read the tables this way:.

The obvious test is to time 100 calls through the gateway, time 100 direct calls, and compare the two medians. That test gives the wrong answer, for two reasons.

The first reason is noise. OpenAI's own response time moved by hundreds of milliseconds between calls in our runs. The direct call's p95 was 1,047 to 1,233 ms against a median near 800 ms. A gateway that adds 20 ms is hidden inside that spread unless the test removes it.

The second reason is the network path to OpenAI. It does not stay the same between a direct client and a gateway, and that difference can be larger than the gateway itself.

According to recent reports, api.openai.com resolves to more than one address. From our network, DNS returned two Cloudflare addresses, and one was much farther away than the other. We measured both with a script that pins one address at a time:.

Sources indicate that on a connection that is already open, both addresses answer in the same time. On a newly introduced connection, the far address adds about 250 ms, because the TCP and TLS handshakes take that much longer.

A gateway keeps its connection to OpenAI open between calls. It pays the setup once and then stays on whichever address it reached first. A client that opens a upcoming connection for each call pays the setup again on every call. How much it pays depends on which address DNS returns that time.

It has been revealed that node's built-in fetch closes an idle connection after about 4 seconds. So a test client that calls OpenAI every few seconds reconnects on almost every call. In our first, uncontrolled run, the Langfuse gateway came out 43 ms faster than calling OpenAI directly. A gateway cannot be faster than the call it forwards. The direct client paid for new connections, and the gateway did not.

The fix has two parts. First, pin api.openai.com to one address on every path. In Docker, that is an extra_hosts entry on each gateway container:.

Second, let the direct client keep its connection open, as a gateway does. With undici, the HTTP client behind Node's fetch, that is a custom Agent:.

It has been revealed that we then listed each container's open connections to confirm that every path used the same address. The edge-check script is in the repository linked at the end, and it takes about a minute to run from your own network.

In a recent development, this advice also applies outside benchmarks. If your app calls OpenAI directly from Node, keep the connection open between calls. Otherwise some of your calls pay the handshake, and on a far address that costs about 250 ms.

Each test sent 150 rounds after 5 warm-up rounds. One round calls OpenAI directly and through each gateway, once without streaming and once with streaming. The order rotates every round, so no path always goes first or last.

For each round, the script takes the gateway's time minus the direct call's time in that same round. Calls in one round are made within a few seconds of each other, so a slow moment at OpenAI hits all four paths together and cancels out of the difference. The script then reports the median of the 150 differences.

In a recent development, the interval comes from a bootstrap. The script draws 150 differences at random, with replacement, and takes their median. It repeats that 2,000 times, and the middle 95% of those medians is the interval. This is a shortened version of the script's function:.

Recent findings suggest that an interval that includes zero means the test could not separate the gateway's cost from zero. That is what the Langfuse rows show. It does not prove that the cost is zero.

Every call used OpenAI gpt-6-luna with reasoning_effort: "none", the same short prompt and a cap of 5 output tokens. A short answer keeps the model's own time small, so more of the measured time belongs to the path. Each streamed call measured the time to its first token. Each non-streamed call measured the time to the full response.

All three gateways did real work on every call, which made the comparison fair:.

The three logging levels mapped to these settings:.

According to recent reports, the machine was an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X with 62 GB of RAM, running Fedora Linux and Docker 29.9. All three stacks ran on it at once, and the test was run on 10 November 2026.

LiteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to the full response, but only 9 to 43 ms to the first streamed token. The first token arrives as soon as the model starts to answer, so time spent before that point indicates up in both numbers. The larger cost without streaming suggests that most of LiteLLM's extra time is spent after the model has answered. We did not profile LiteLLM to confirm this.

Industry observers note that logging level made no clear difference for any gateway. Adding LiteLLM's Langfuse callback did not raise its cost. AcruxCore's median rose from 15 ms with logging off to 24 ms with full logging, but its intervals overlap across all three runs. AcruxCore's median is 16 to 24 ms above Langfuse's, and those intervals overlap too, so this test does not rank the two of them.

If 60 ms per call matters to you, as in a chat app that makes several model calls per user message, LiteLLM's cost is real and repeatable. Langfuse and AcruxCore stayed near or within the noise. If your calls take several seconds, any of the three costs less than OpenAI's own variation from one call to the next.

It has been revealed that before you trust a gateway number, your own or anyone else's, check two things. Was each gateway compared with a direct call in the same round? And did the direct client keep its connection open on the same OpenAI address as the gateway? Without both, the result measures the network path and not the gateway.

The scripts, Compose files and raw results are on GitHub: scripts/comparison/langfuse-gateway-vs-litellm-vs-acruxcore.

#115814. Power and cooling limits force AI clusters with 100,000+ accelerators to use multiple data centers

Power and cooling limits force AI clusters with 100,000+ accelerators to use multiple data centers

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The rapid growth of AI clusters is pushing computing infrastructure beyond the physical and power limitations of individual data centers, which creates demand for latest networking architectures capable of connecting compute resources across multiple facilities and even geographical regions.
  • Modern AI clusters typically accommodate more than 100,000 AI accelerators and potentially millions of CPU endpoints, placing tremendous demands on network bandwidth, latency, and congestion management.
  • Industry observers note that traditionally, high-performance computing systems have relied on two major interconnect domains: scale-up and scale-out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The rapid growth of AI clusters is pushing computing infrastructure beyond the physical and power limitations of individual data centers, which creates demand for latest networking architectures capable of connecting compute resources across multiple facilities and even geographical regions. At Supercomputing 2026 (SC26), researchers from The Ohio State University discussed the evolution of high-performance networking technologies. At the conference, they explained how efficient distributed computing at such a scale requires considerably more than faster network connections, highlighting the importance of scale across domains to stretch workloads across different data centers in separate geographical regions.

Modern AI clusters typically accommodate more than 100,000 AI accelerators and potentially millions of CPU endpoints, placing tremendous demands on network bandwidth, latency, and congestion management. Meanwhile, an accelerator's computational performance continues to increase faster than communication capabilities, which means that faster AI GPUs do not necessarily deliver proportional improvements in application performance. As a result, the efficiency of network infrastructure determines how effectively large-scale AI systems can use their computational resources.

Industry observers note that traditionally, high-performance computing systems have relied on two major interconnect domains: scale-up and scale-out. Scale-up networks connect processors and accelerators within tightly integrated systems using technologies like AMD's Infinity Fabric, Intel's UPI, Nvidia's NVLink, or emerging alternatives such as UALink. Scale-out networks, which typically rely on Ethernet, InfiniBand, HPE Slingshot, or, more recently, Ultra Ethernet, connect individual servers or rack-scale systems into larger clusters. These interconnects have different requirements for bandwidth, latency, and scalability, which is why they serve different purposes.

Sources indicate that however, the massive size and power consumption of modern AI clusters create demand for a third interconnect domain, known as scale-across. Unlike scale-out networks, which typically connect systems within a single data center, scale-across architectures extend high-performance connectivity between different buildings, campuses, or even regions.

Such an approach enables operators to combine computational and other resources from multiple locations to achieve a certain level of performance rather than to bring an excessive number of accelerators to a single data center, which may be hard, or even impossible, due to power availability, cooling requirements, or physical space constraints.

The transition toward scale-across architectures has already begun. Google introduced its Virgo network architecture earlier this year to support AI workloads that exceed the space and power capacity of individual data centers. The company intends to treat an entire campus of computing facilities as a single system, albeit with specialized networks for communication between accelerators, servers, and data centers. Cisco and Marvell are also developing technologies for scale-across deployments, including high-capacity routers, switching chips, and optical interconnects designed to connect geographically distributed clusters.

Sources indicate that extending AI infrastructure beyond individual facilities introduces substantial technical challenges. While modern scale-up networks offer extremely high bandwidth and low latency over relatively short distances, communication between data centers must contend with the physical limitations of long-distance connections. Even optical networks cannot eliminate propagation delays, whereas congestion, packet loss, and synchronization overhead can further reduce effective performance. Consequently, connecting two large GPU clusters with high-speed links does not necessarily make them behave like one tightly integrated computing system.

These challenges are particularly vital for AI training, where accelerators frequently exchange model parameters, gradients, and intermediate results. Large-scale workloads require efficient collective communications, as delays that affect individual accelerators dramatically reduce the performance of the entire cluster. Therefore, the efficiency of distributed computing depends not only on raw network bandwidth, but also on network topology, congestion management, communication protocols, and software implementations.

Sources indicate that to address these limitations, network adapters and switches are becoming more sophisticated than ever. Modern network interface controllers can perform Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) operations without continuous CPU involvement, whereas technologies such as HPE Slingshot hardware collectives and Nvidia SHARP can offload certain communication operations to the network infrastructure itself. SmartNICs and data processing units further reduce the burden on host processors as they handle selected network and infrastructure functions in dedicated hardware. Such capabilities can improve efficiency of distributed applications without necessarily requiring faster physical interconnects.

In a recent development, interestingly, software plays an equally important role in the performance of large-scale AI infrastructure, as communication frameworks like libfabric, MPI, or UCX determine how applications exchange data and use the capabilities of modern network adapters. Also, GPU-aware communication and technologies like GPUDirect RDMA can eliminate unnecessary transfers through host memory, while optimized collective operations can reduce communication overhead across large numbers of accelerators, according to the researchers.

In a recent development, the growing complexity of AI infrastructure also changes how operators should evaluate network performance. Although the industry continues to introduce faster interconnect technologies, including versions of GbE with nominal bandwidths of 800 Gb/s and 1.6 Tb/s, peak transfer rates alone do not fully describe the capabilities of a given system because the performance of actual applications depends on multiple factors, including how effectively network hardware and software cooperate to transfer data, prevent congestion, and synchronize computations across thousands of processors.

According to recent reports, ultimately, the emergence of scale-across interconnection architectures reflects a fundamental change in the design of AI infrastructure. As the computational capabilities of individual accelerators increase and AI clusters expand beyond individual facilities, efficient communication becomes just as important as processor performance. As a result, the next generation of AI systems will depend not only on faster AI accelerators or CPUs, but also on sophisticated network adapters, switches, and, perhaps more importantly, software that can unite geographically distributed computational resources without excessive communication overhead.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players have found that music in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+’s fresh GTA 6-themed secret run was made with Suno, as the free DLC sits at Overwhelmingly Negative recent reviews on Steam.

Creator Edmund McMillen has since stated he had no idea the music was AI-generated, with publisher Nicalis now patching it out of the game.

The run arrived in the same enhancement that brought Repentance+ to PS5, Xbox, and Switch 2 on November 19, a release date publisher Nicalis picked to go head-to-head with GTA 6.

Entering the seed V1CE BSMT unlocks a Vice City-inspired daily run with its own soundtrack, made up of seven songs plus a handful of intros and outros.

A player on the Binding of Isaac subreddit extracted the run’s music from the game files and found several tracks still carrying metadata reading “made with suno,” along with links to the songs on Suno’s site.

Industry observers note that the metadata on one track shows it was created on October 30, 2026, less than three weeks before the revision went live. Other players have since checked the files and confirmed the find.

It has been revealed that the run itself is credited to a modder known as Mr. Headcrab, who the original poster says is “staunchly anti-AI” and had no idea the music was generated.

Valve requires developers to disclose AI-generated content on a game’s Steam page, but Repentance+’s store listing makes no mention of it.

The DLC currently sits at Overwhelmingly Negative recent reviews, with only 10% of 908 reviews from the past 30 days positive, though the same enhancement has also been blamed for breaking mods and causing crashes.

For some fans, the AI music is the final straw. “They used AI when synthwave is like… the easiest genre to make,” one player wrote, in a comment with dozens of upvotes.

Sources indicate that the community-run Isaac wiki has since added a note flagging the AI-generated tracks. Nicalis has yet to comment on the music or add a disclosure to the Steam page.

McMillen addressed the backlash on X, making it clear the music had been added without his knowledge.

“Woke up to a sh*t show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run,” he wrote. “Looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.”.

Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.

Within hours, Nicalis pushed a new build of Repentance+, listing the “removal of generated music files” at the top of its patch notes, alongside fixes for mods broken by the launch revision.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games has been accused of tracing a furry artist’s illustration for a decal on a custom submachine gun players can earn in GTA 6.

Sources indicate that the gun comes from a random encounter with Chase, a fox-suited character cornered by police. Players can break through the blockade, lose the cops, and help Chase and another furry escape to the Furverts’ compound.

Chase offers the custom SMG as an alternative to cash for helping them escape. The encounter had already drawn comparisons to a real-life fursuit after players noticed shooting-star markings on Chase’s knees that resemble those on FoxiFelix’s suit.

Industry observers note that on November 21, X user Glacius shared what they described as artwork pulled from GTA 6’s game files, including a view of the graphics used on the custom SMG. In a follow-up linking to furry artist GabyT’s work, Glacius asked, “IT WAS TRACED????”.

In a recent development, rockstar definitely had an insider for GTA 6. Datamined furry artwork! pic.twitter.com/MjXvUz1PCq.

Industry observers note that gabyT posted the illustration on December 8, 2021, nearly five years before GTA 6’s release. The portrait and the weapon decal both show a character with its head turned to the side, a half-lidded eye, and white fur flaring out around a dark muzzle. The version on the gun uses muddier colors and shows the character holding a bone in its mouth.

According to recent reports, commission done to Markwrc! ✅Want to see more content? Stay tuned on my social medias and watch the lives on Twitch too! ✨💻✨#wacomart #digitalart #drawing #illustration #furry #furryart #furrywolf #fantasy #animal #artwork pic.twitter.com/5dxAfFsd3X.

Sockz the Puppet posted a video overlaying the two images, then shared a revised comparison after lining them up on a computer. “I hope the og artist was aware and gave permission,” they wrote.

bro what is this :/ I hope rockstar paid for this? https://t.co/kh35xMfHU2 pic.twitter.com/fIfvVX9vSM.

It has been revealed that the replies were split over how closely the drawings matched. X user Eli Bunny said the decal looked traced and wanted to know whether Rockstar worked with GabyT. Another user, Stick, said the images “barely line up” and described the overlap as “minor similarities.”.

In a recent development, in a reply discussing how the artwork could have made it into the game, Sockz argued that the publisher was responsible for what it shipped. “When you publish something, it becomes your responsibility,” they wrote.

According to recent reports, it remains unclear whether Rockstar contacted GabyT or had permission to use the illustration. Rockstar has yet to publicly address the tracing allegation.
